domain_label: Turlock Professional & Financial Services — Market, Demand & Saturation Economics
purpose: A method for sizing and reading the 14-business independent Professional & Financial services market in Turlock, CA: quantifying the demand base (resident/household transaction pool, the farm economy, and the four language/trust communities), explaining why the count saturates near 14 independents, separating the commission/fee mechanics by sub-category (insurance, real estate, accounting/tax, notary/immigration-doc), locating leakage to Modesto and online, mapping competitive structure and white-space, and expressing every revenue, margin and market-size figure strictly as a labeled benchmark estimate (industry per-unit benchmark x an observable size signal) rather than as a stated fact about any named business.
assumptions: no per-business revenue dataset is supplied; every dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate, never an actual reported figure for any named business (CalWest, Berger & Company, Vega's, etc.)
the universe is the 14 verified Turlock independents in businesses.json (captives, national chains, solo enrolled agents, and bundled functions excluded), as of the 2026-06-30 snapshot

city/county/state/industry figures (population 72,502, median household income $82,995, license/bond fees, statutory fee caps, commission-rate norms) are cited public facts or explicitly labeled derivations

format-level revenue bands are published industry per-unit benchmarks (commission rate, returns-per-preparer, fee-per-return, per-side commission) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal (lines of business, firm-name structure, tenure, inferred headcount), tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path
Modesto (county seat, ~15 minutes north) is the regional professional anchor that caps Turlock's complex/high-value ceiling while commodity work leaks online
coverage is reported as a FLOOR, not a ceiling; the single highest-leverage confirmation is CA DOI / DRE / CTEC license rosters for the 95380/95382 ZIPs joined to CDTFA/BLS occupational data
exclusions: per-sub-category software stacks, carrier/lender/MLS sourcing, and licensing operations — covered by the supply-chain/operations KB
per-sub-category unit-economics, cost-structure and go/no-go business-model detail — covered by the business-models KB
any claim of an actual, reported, or audited dollar revenue for a named business
captive insurance offices, national tax chains, and solo enrolled agents, which are outside the independents-only catalog
individual pricing tactics, producer-recruiting, or marketing execution for a specific operator

competency_questions.question: What demand base generates Turlock's professional/financial transaction pool, and how large is the household and farm-economy substrate as a labeled estimate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_BASE names the 72,502 residents / 25,365 households / $82,995 median income substrate and FARM_ECONOMY_DEMAND ties the ag/trucking/crop base to commercial-lines and bookkeeping demand, both tagged with source confidence

competency_questions.question: How do Turlock's four language/trust communities raise demand for multilingual professional services above what population alone predicts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMUNITY_TRUST_DEMAND ties the Assyrian (~20k), Mexican-American, Portuguese/Azorean and Punjabi/Sikh communities to the tax/notary/immigration/translation formats they anchor and explains the relationship-and-language defensibility

competency_questions.question: Why is licensed-professional supply, not capital or premises, the binding constraint on how many firms the market sustains?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LICENSE_LABOR_SUPPLY names the CPA/EA/CTEC, CA DOI producer, DRE broker and notary/immigration-consultant gates as friction-not-wall and frames credentialed labor meeting a bounded pool as the equilibrium-setting scarcity

competency_questions.question: How is the local transaction pool (returns, policies, home sales) sized as a labeled estimate, and why is it calendar-locked and finite?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRANSACTION_POOL derives the bounded annual count of returns, in-force policies and ~once-a-decade home sales from the household base, tagged estimate-not-actual with the roster/CDTFA confirmation path

competency_questions.question: How do the four sub-categories monetize (carrier commission, per-side commission, fee-per-return, capped notary fee), and how does that shape revenue?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMISSION_FEE_MECHANICS states the commission-funded vs fee-funded split and the per-unit benchmarks (P&C 8-20% of premium, CA RE ~5.47%, fee-per-return, ~$15/signature cap) that drive each sub-category's revenue

competency_questions.question: How is a per-format benchmark revenue band built so it is an honest estimate and never a stated fact for a named business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_REVENUE_BANDS states the benchmark x size-signal method, gives each sub-category band, and tags every band estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

competency_questions.question: Why must high gross commission/GCI/fees never be read as high net income across these sub-categories?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GROSS_NET_GAP pairs each gross band with its labor-and-license cost reality (payroll ~40-60% of revenue, producer/agent splits, E&O, software) so a high-gross format is never mistaken for high net

competency_questions.question: Why does a ~73k town support roughly 14 nameable independents — not 30, not 5 — and what forces set that equilibrium?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EQUILIBRIUM_COUNT names the bounded demand pool, two-sided leakage, licensing friction and incumbent referral networks as caps, and the four-community demand as the one expander, tying the ~14 count to them

competency_questions.question: How saturated is each sub-category once captives and chains are counted, and why is every density figure a floor?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SATURATION_DENSITY gives the per-10k independent-only density (insurance 0.83, accounting 0.41, RE 0.55, notary 0.14) and COVERAGE_FLOOR explains why each is a lower bound on true supply

competency_questions.question: How do leakage to Modesto and to online players cap both the top and the bottom of the independent middle?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEAKAGE_MODESTO_ONLINE explains complex/high-value work migrating ~15 miles to Modesto and commodity/price-sensitive work leaking online, leaving independents the relationship-and-language middle

competency_questions.question: Where is each sub-category on the crowded-vs-white-space spectrum, and how is the notary/immigration white-space monetizable only through bundling?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INSURANCE_STRUCTURE, REALESTATE_STRUCTURE, ACCOUNTING_STRUCTURE and MULTISERVICIOS_WHITESPACE each give a saturated/crowded/moderate/white-space read, with the Vega's bundling model and the notario-fraud scope cap explained

competency_questions.question: How is an entry go/no-go verdict reached for a sub-category, what regulatory-scope or referral-moat gate overrides a demand-true opening, and how are the reads refreshed when the figures change?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ENTRY_GO_NOGO composes the saturation read, leakage, white-space and the regulatory-scope/referral-moat gate into a verdict that refuses demand-true but gated additions, and MARKET_REVIEW_LOOP defines the refresh cadence and the material-change triggers (license-roster release, fee-schedule change, demographic refresh, rate-cycle move) that re-run the pool and saturation reads

glossary.definition: The estimated bounded annual count of returns, in-force policies and home sales the ~25,365-household, 72,502-resident Turlock base generates; households transact (file annually, renew policies yearly, sell a home roughly once a decade) on a calendar-locked cadence, making the pool finite and a labeled estimate, not a measured figure.

The honest revenue-estimation method used throughout: take a published per-unit industry benchmark (commission rate, returns-per-preparer, fee-per-return, per-side commission) and scale it by an observable Turlock size signal (lines of business, firm-name structure, tenure, inferred headcount), yielding a band tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level.

The split in how each sub-category gets paid: insurance and real estate are commission-funded (the carrier or the sale proceeds pay, not the client directly), while accounting/tax and notary/immigration are fee-funded (the client pays a fee or a statutorily capped charge); this drives revenue smoothness and seasonality.

The distinction that high commission/GCI/fees are gross, while net income is far lower after the labor-and-license cost stack (payroll ~40-60% of revenue, producer/agent splits, E&O, software/data subscriptions); conflating gross with net is the most common revenue misread in this sector.

The rule that the catalog counts only verifiable independents, so every per-10k density figure is a lower bound on true supply; captive insurance offices, national tax chains, solo enrolled agents, and notary/translation functions bundled inside other businesses are known to exist and are not fully counted.

The two-sided drain that caps the independent middle: complex/high-value work (audits, commercial-risk placement, HNW tax planning) migrates ~15 miles to Modesto's larger firms, while commodity/price-sensitive work (simple returns, commodity auto/home, simple home sales) leaks to TurboTax/Policygenius/Redfin-style online players.

The binding entry barrier in a trust/referral economy: incumbents (insurance agencies '20+ years in Turlock', family RE firms) hold the in-force book and referral graph, raising the effective cost of new entry well above the licensing cost; the moat is the book/referral graph, not the license.

The immigrant-serving format (Vega's Professional Services archetype) that stacks tax + notary + bookkeeping + payroll + real estate + translation + mobile service to smooth tax seasonality and serve a referral-dependent, often Spanish-speaking base; the notary line alone does not pencil under the fee cap, so viability depends on the bundle.

The CA statutory prohibition (B&P 22440 et seq.) on a notary publico / immigration consultant giving legal advice; only attorneys or DOJ/EOIR-accredited reps may, which caps a Vega's-type shop to form-filling, translation and notarization and makes the attorney/accredited-rep referral a structural part of the workflow.

A per-capita density read: catalog count divided by 7.25 ten-thousands of residents (insurance 6/7.25=0.83, accounting 3/7.25=0.41, real estate 4/7.25=0.55, notary 1/7.25=0.14), set against coarse national benchmarks and always read as a floor because captives, chains and bundled functions are uncounted.

source_registry.description: labeled benchmark estimates and cited public facts for the Turlock independent Professional & Financial services market, grounded in the professional_financial deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md), its reconciled brief (reconciled.md), and the 14-business source dataset (businesses.json); demand sizing uses ACS household counts and per-household transaction frequency, format revenue bands use published insurance-commission, returns-per-preparer, fee-per-return and per-side commission benchmarks, and saturation/leakage reads use census population and national agencies/firms-per-capita figures
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Census QuickFacts 2024 (Turlock 72,502 pop, 25,365 households, $82,995 median HH income, 46% Hispanic, Assyrian ~20k); KQED/Wikipedia (Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, Punjabi/Sikh communities); IBISWorld/Census (~128k tax-prep firms; ~400k insurance agencies); industry commission norms (P&C 8-20% of premium; CA total RE commission ~5.47%); NSA/NAR/Indeed fee and per-side benchmarks; CA SoS/AB-2217 notary and immigration-consultant fee caps and bonds; LoopNet/CommercialCafe 2025/26 office rent; Redfin/Turlock Journal median home ~$465-475k; CA DOI/DRE/CTEC rosters and CDTFA/BLS (the confirmation sources); professional_financial DEEPDIVE.md, reconciled.md, businesses.json

nodes.definition: Catalog the structural demand substrate the 14 independents share: 72,502 residents, 25,365 households, a $82,995 median household income (county $81,468) and 68.9% family households, a working-and-middle-income, family-heavy population. Nearly every household files a return, carries mandatory auto/home insurance, and transacts a home roughly once a decade, so the household count, not the resident count alone, sets the calendar-locked demand the professional/financial firms compete over. This is a license-and-relationship economy with near-zero cost of goods sold, so demand, not supply chain, is the binding sizing input. The substrate is a cited public fact (Census QuickFacts 2024); converting it to dollar revenue is a downstream estimate.

excluded: community-specific anchoring (its own node)
the farm-economy commercial base (its own node)
converting the base to a transaction or dollar pool

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a population, household, or income figure is refreshed

pros.claim: Anchoring the market in the household count, not the resident count, matches the calendar-locked way returns, policies and sales are generated
pros.example: 25,365 households filing annually sets tax demand a resident headcount would misstate

cons.claim: A median-income, household-count substrate hides the bimodal price sensitivity within the base
cons.example: cash-paying immigrant filers and fee-tolerant farm clients sit in the same household count but transact very differently

failure_modes: sizing on residents instead of households and overstating the pool
treating a single median income as the whole price-sensitivity picture
acceptance_tests: the resident count, household count, and median household income are each stated with the Census source and tagged as cited public facts, and the calendar-locked household-transaction framing is named
revisit_triggers: a census or ACS demographic refresh
a household-count or median-income update
a major employer opens or closes and shifts the income base

nodes.definition: Explain Turlock's defining demand expander: four layered language/trust communities each anchor multilingual professional services a demographically average 73k town would not sustain. The Assyrian community (~20,000, about a quarter of town) plus a long-established Portuguese/Azorean community, a large Mexican-American community (the 46% Hispanic base), and a Punjabi/Sikh South-Asian community create demand for culturally matched tax, notary, immigration-doc and translation work. This is the genuine white-space and defensibility of the sector — the multiservicios/gestoria format embodied by Vega's Professional Services — and the hardest demand for Modesto and online players to take, because it runs on language and trust, not price or scale. Community share is a cited public fact; its conversion to revenue is an estimate.

included: the Assyrian, Mexican-American, Portuguese/Azorean and Punjabi/Sikh communities
the formats each anchors (tax, notary, immigration, translation)
excluded: the dollar size of each community's spend
the regulatory scope cap on the notary line (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a community share or migration trend changes

pros.claim: Mapping community to format explains demand national density models under-predict
pros.example: the multilingual tax/notary/translation demand at Vega's makes sense only against the four-community substrate

cons.claim: Community share is a crude proxy for professional-service spend, which differs by language access and price sensitivity
cons.example: a large but cash-and-price-sensitive immigrant base supports many low-ticket bundled shops but caps their per-unit revenue

failure_modes: assuming community share converts linearly to professional-service revenue
ignoring that the demand is monetizable only through bundling under the fee cap
acceptance_tests: each of the four communities is tied to at least one anchored professional format with its cited share, and the language-and-trust defensibility versus Modesto/online is stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: an ancestry/demographic data refresh
a community grows or contracts via migration
a community-anchored multiservicios format opens or closes

nodes.definition: Isolate the farm-economy commercial demand that wraps the Turlock professional/financial market and over-indexes its commercial lines. The substantial Stanislaus County farm/trucking/retail/self-employed base drives ag, commercial-auto/trucking and crop insurance lines, quarterly bookkeeping and payroll, and farm/business tax and audit work — non-discretionary, fee-tolerant, sticky commercial demand that a purely residential town would not generate. This is the defensible business middle for insurance agencies (CalWest, Winton-Ireland, Strom & Green) and full CPA firms (Berger & Company, Wahl, Willemse & Wilson) that neither online players nor distant Modesto firms easily serve. The farm base is a cited structural fact; its per-firm revenue contribution is an estimate.

included: the commercial insurance and business-accounting demand it drives
excluded: residential/household demand (DEMAND_BASE)
the per-sub-category revenue bands (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a farm-economy or commercial-base figure changes

pros.claim: Naming the farm-economy base explains the commercial-lines and business-accounting depth a residential read would miss
pros.example: crop and commercial-trucking insurance demand supports multi-line independents a pure personal-lines town could not

cons.claim: Farm/commercial demand is cyclical and concentration-prone, exposing firms to a narrow client mix
cons.example: a few large farm accounts can dominate a CPA firm's book and concentrate its risk

failure_modes: treating the market as purely residential and undercounting commercial-lines demand
ignoring the cyclicality of ag/commercial demand
acceptance_tests: the farm/trucking/crop commercial base is tied to specific commercial insurance and business-accounting demand, and its sticky/fee-tolerant character is named as the defensible business middle
revisit_triggers: a county agricultural-economy shift
a major ag employer or processor opens or closes
a crop-insurance or commercial-lines regulatory change

nodes.definition: Frame the supply side: the binding constraint on how many firms the market sustains is licensed-professional supply meeting a bounded demand pool, not capital or premises. Capex is trivial across all four sub-categories and office rent is modest (~$20/SF/yr), so what is scarce is a credentialed CPA/EA, a seasoned producer with carrier appointments, or a DRE broker willing to hang a shingle. The licensing gates — CPA/EA/CTEC for tax, CA DOI producer for insurance, DRE broker for real estate, notary commission plus $15k bond and $100k immigration-consultant bond — are real but not prohibitive (a 60-hour CTEC course, a DRE exam, a producer pre-license course), so they slow rather than stop entry. That friction, not a wall, is why density sits near rather than far above benchmark.

included: credentialed labor as the scarce input
excluded: the regulatory scope cap on legal advice (its own node)
the demand-side transaction pool

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a licensing gate or credential-pipeline cost changes

pros.claim: Identifying licensed labor as the scarce input correctly locates the equilibrium constraint away from capital
pros.example: trivial capex but a multi-week-to-months license gate explains why entry is throttled, not blocked

cons.claim: Treating licensing as mere friction can understate carrier-appointment and referral barriers that compound it
cons.example: a newly licensed producer still cannot quote competitively without carrier appointments or a cluster

failure_modes: over-weighting capital/premises as the constraint when labor is binding
treating the license as the whole moat and ignoring the referral/appointment barrier
acceptance_tests: each sub-category's licensing gate is named with its public cost/requirement and framed as friction-not-wall, and credentialed labor meeting a bounded pool is stated as the equilibrium-setting scarcity
revisit_triggers: a licensing requirement, bond, or fee schedule changes
a credential pipeline (CTEC/DRE/DOI) shifts in cost or duration
a carrier-appointment or cluster-access norm changes

nodes.definition: Size the bounded annual transaction pool as a labeled estimate: ~25,365 households generate on the order of tens of thousands of tax returns, a comparable count of in-force personal-lines policies (auto/home legally or contractually mandatory), and home sales at roughly a once-a-decade per-household cadence (on the order of a few thousand sales a year county-wide, a smaller slice in Turlock). This calendar-locked, finite pool — Jan-Apr tax crush, annual policy renewals, a thin 2024-25 home-sale market — is the demand ceiling the 14 independents share; it is explicitly an estimate, not a measured figure, and its single best confirmation is CA DOI/DRE/CTEC license rosters joined to CDTFA/BLS occupational data. Farm/commercial and community demand partly overlap and partly add to this resident pool rather than stacking cleanly on top of it.

excluded: the commission/fee mechanics that monetize the pool (its own node)
per-format revenue bands

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a household count, frequency assumption, or roster/CDTFA dataset is refreshed

pros.claim: A transparent household-x-frequency method gives a defensible pool ceiling without quoting any business
pros.example: stating returns ~= households filing and sales ~= households/10 lets a reader audit the estimate end to end

cons.claim: Per-household frequency is a national-ish assumption that an atypical, multilingual, farm-heavy town can violate
cons.example: self-employed and farm households file more complex and more frequent filings than the once-a-year baseline

failure_modes: presenting the pool as a measured figure rather than an estimate
stacking community and farm demand fully on top of the resident pool and double-counting
acceptance_tests: the pool is stated as a household-x-frequency estimate for returns, policies and sales, with the calendar-locked finiteness, a confidence level, and the roster/CDTFA confirmation path, tagged estimate-not-actual
revisit_triggers: an ACS household-count refresh
a CA DOI/DRE/CTEC roster release
CDTFA/BLS occupational data becomes available
a home-sale-volume cycle shift

nodes.definition: Establish how each sub-category converts a transaction into revenue, because the payment mechanism, not foot traffic, drives the bands. Insurance is commission-funded: the carrier pays ~12-15% new / 2-12% renewal on personal lines, P&C broadly 8-20% of premium, and producers keep ~30-90% of agency commission. Real estate is commission-funded out of sale proceeds at ~5.47% total CA commission (listing side ~2.73%), ~$11k-$15k per side to the agent on a ~$465-475k median home, typically split 70/30 with the broker. Accounting/tax is fee-funded: ~$200-$600+ per CPA-firm 1040 by complexity, plus recurring bookkeeping/payroll. Notary/immigration is fee-funded but statutorily capped at ~$15/signature and $15 per immigration form set, with loan signings (~$75-$200) the real margin driver. Commission rates are sourced facts; their application to any Turlock book is an estimate.

included: the per-unit benchmark rates per sub-category
excluded: the assembled revenue bands (its own node)
the cost stack that turns gross into net (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a commission rate, fee cap, or split norm changes

pros.claim: Separating the payment mechanism per sub-category prevents a one-size revenue model across very different economics
pros.example: a commission-funded renewal book smooths insurance revenue while a fee-capped notary line stays volume-thin

cons.claim: Published rate ranges are wide, so applying a single rate to any book overstates precision
cons.example: an 8-20% P&C commission band spans more than 2x and cannot pin a firm's revenue

failure_modes: applying a sourced commission rate to a named book as if it produced a stated revenue
ignoring the producer/agent split that diverts much of gross commission away from the firm
acceptance_tests: each sub-category's payment mechanism is stated with its cited per-unit benchmark (P&C 8-20% of premium, CA RE ~5.47%, fee-per-return, ~$15/signature cap) and the commission-rate-is-fact-but-application-is-estimate caveat is named
revisit_triggers: a commission-rate norm or statutory fee cap changes
a producer/agent split norm shifts
the median home price moves the per-side figure

nodes.definition: Build the per-sub-category gross revenue bands that are the primary, most defensible revenue view, every one a labeled estimate (published benchmark x observable Turlock size signal), never an actual figure for a named business. Representative bands: solo/small CPA (Charles Strand profile, ~150-300 returns x ~$300 avg fee plus light bookkeeping) ~$60k-$250k, medium confidence; full CPA firm (Berger / Wahl, Willemse & Wilson profile, 3-6 staff, audit/advisory) ~$400k-$1.2M+, low-medium confidence and the sector's lowest-confidence band because staff count is unknown; insurance agency (book x blended commission, multi-line/ag/20+yr tenure like CalWest at the top) ~$300k-$2M+ commission revenue, low-medium confidence; real-estate brokerage GCI ~$150k-$1M+ with per-agent net often under $50k-$110k (a national NAR/Indeed benchmark, not a Turlock fact); notary line alone ~$20k-$80k, bundled multiservicios total ~$80k-$200k+. Each band must travel with its method, public source, confidence word and the gross-not-net caveat.

included: the confidence word and confirmation path per band
excluded: the detailed cost stack (its own node)
the confidence-ladder ranking across bands (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark source or measured size signal changes

pros.claim: Per-sub-category bands anchored to published per-unit benchmarks give a planning estimate without quoting any operator
pros.example: a solo-CPA band from returns-per-preparer x avg fee is auditable and business-agnostic

cons.claim: Bands rest on national benchmarks and unobserved size signals, so any single firm can sit far outside its band
cons.example: a multi-partner LLP's actual revenue could exceed the full-CPA-firm top or fall below its floor depending on unknown headcount

failure_modes: attaching a band to a named business as if it were that business's revenue
dropping the confidence word so the lowest-confidence full-CPA band reads as solid
acceptance_tests: each sub-category has a labeled gross band derived as benchmark x a stated size signal, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence word and confirmation path, and the full-CPA-firm band is flagged as the lowest-confidence in the sector
revisit_triggers: a published benchmark source updates
an observable size signal (lines, staff, tenure) is measured for a firm type
CA DOI/DRE/CTEC roster or CDTFA data lands

nodes.definition: Correct the most common revenue misread in this sector: high commission/GCI/fees are gross, not net. Because true COGS is near-zero, this is a labor-and-license cost structure in which the cost stack (licensed labor first, then occupancy, then software/data subscriptions, then insurance/bond/licensing) consumes most of gross. Payroll commonly runs ~40-60% of revenue for professional-services firms; insurance carries E&O ~$500-$1,000/employee/yr plus an agency-management-system subscription; pro tax software (Drake/ProSeries to Lacerte ~$1,800-$2,300/user, UltraTax ~$2,500+) is the signature recurring input; real-estate brokerages give up the agent split (often 70/30) plus MLS dues, E&O and marketing. So an insurance agency's high commission revenue or a brokerage's high GCI must never be read as high net income. Every high-gross band must be paired with this cost reality.

included: the payroll ~40-60% and key software/E&O/split costs
excluded: the detailed per-firm cost-structure (business-models KB)
the gross band values themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cost-stack ratio or software/split benchmark changes

pros.claim: Pairing every gross band with the cost stack stops a high-commission or high-GCI figure being read as profit
pros.example: a brokerage's $1M GCI is mostly paid out in agent splits before any net reaches the broker

cons.claim: Cost-stack ratios are themselves benchmark estimates, so the net read is a band on a band
cons.example: payroll at 40% vs 60% of revenue produces materially different net with no firm-level data to choose

failure_modes: quoting a gross band as if it were net income
omitting the producer/agent split so commission/GCI looks fully retained
acceptance_tests: each high-gross sub-category band is paired with its labor-and-license cost reality (payroll ~40-60%, splits, E&O, software) and the gross-is-not-net rule is stated explicitly
revisit_triggers: a software/data subscription price hike
a payroll-ratio or E&O benchmark update
a producer/agent split norm shifts

nodes.definition: Rank the revenue bands by how far each benchmark must be stretched to a single unnamed Turlock firm, so a reader knows which numbers to trust least. Highest confidence: the insurance commission rate and the CA real-estate commission percentage (sourced industry facts). Medium: the solo/small-CPA band (returns-per-preparer x avg fee is a tight benchmark) and the notary-line-alone band (volume x a statutory fee cap). Lowest: the full-CPA-firm band (~$400k-$1.2M+) because it rests on a staff count that is unknown, and the bundled multiservicios total because volume is unknown. Every low-confidence band carries an explicit confirmation path — CA DOI/DRE/CTEC license rosters joined to CDTFA/BLS data — that would convert it from a benchmark estimate into a measured figure. The ladder governs how much downstream planning may lean on each band.

included: the confidence ranking across the bands
the lowest-confidence flags (full CPA firm, bundled total)
the confirmation path per low-confidence band
excluded: the band values themselves (their own node)
the honesty-labeling discipline (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a confirmation dataset or benchmark changes a band's confidence

pros.claim: Ranking bands by confidence stops a reader treating the lowest-confidence full-CPA band as equal to the sourced commission rate
pros.example: marking the full-CPA band low-confidence-staff-unknown prevents it being cited without caveat

cons.claim: A confidence ladder can read as hedging that lowers the analysis's perceived usefulness
cons.example: a reader wanting one revenue number is frustrated that the most relevant band is the least confident

failure_modes: citing the full-CPA-firm band without its staff-count-unknown caveat
treating all bands as equally reliable
acceptance_tests: the bands are ranked by confidence, the full-CPA-firm and bundled-total bands are flagged lowest-confidence, and each low-confidence band names the roster/CDTFA confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a confirmation dataset (roster, CDTFA) lands and upgrades a band
a new benchmark tightens or loosens a band's confidence

nodes.definition: Read saturation by setting each sub-category's catalog count against population as a per-10k density, with the population base of 72,502 ~= 7.25 ten-thousands. Insurance 6/7.25 = 0.83 per 10k (slightly below the coarse ~1.0-1.3 generic benchmark on independents alone, but saturated once captives are counted); accounting/tax 3/7.25 = 0.41 (at/near the ~0.38 US tax-prep benchmark on independents alone, undercounting chains and solo EAs); real estate 4/7.25 = 0.55 at the brokerage-brand level (white-space at brand level, crowded at the agent level where hundreds of DRE agents county-wide is the binding figure); notary/immigration 1/7.25 = 0.14 (apparent white-space, almost certainly undercounted because the function is bundled inside tax shops and multiservicios). Every figure is a labeled estimate and a floor.

excluded: why coverage is a floor (its own node)
the competitive-structure reads per sub-category (their own nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a catalog count, roster, or per-capita benchmark changes

pros.claim: A per-10k density table makes each sub-category's saturation legible against a national benchmark
pros.example: insurance 0.83 vs ~1.0-1.3 reads as slightly-below on independents alone, flagging the captive undercount

cons.claim: National per-capita benchmarks are coarse with mismatched denominators, so a density read is order-of-magnitude
cons.example: the ~400k-agencies-over-333M insurance benchmark is too rough to call exact saturation

failure_modes: reading a brokerage-brand count as the full real-estate saturation picture when agent density is the binding figure
treating an independent-only density as total supply
acceptance_tests: each sub-category has a per-10k density derived from the catalog count and the 7.25 base, set against its benchmark with a saturated/near/white-space read, and the agent-vs-brand distinction is made for real estate
revisit_triggers: a sub-category firm opens or closes in the catalog
a license-roster release reveals captive/chain/solo supply
a national agencies/firms-per-capita benchmark updates

nodes.definition: Enforce the coverage discipline: the catalog of 14 counts only verifiable independents, so every per-10k density figure is a lower bound on true supply. Known-but-uncounted supply includes captive insurance offices (State Farm/Farmers/Allstate), national tax chains (H&R Block/Liberty/Jackson Hewitt), solo enrolled agents and cash storefront preparers, and notary/translation functions bundled inside multiservicios/check-cashing storefronts. This is exactly why insurance reads 'slightly below' the benchmark on independents (0.83/10k) yet is saturated in reality once captives are added, and why notary's apparent 0.14/10k white-space is an undercount. The undercount is acknowledged but not quantified — a known, directional gap — and resolving it requires the CA DOI/DRE/CTEC rosters for the 95380/95382 ZIPs.

included: the directional-not-quantified character of the undercount
excluded: the density figures themselves (their own node)
the leakage mechanism (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a roster or captive/chain census becomes available

pros.claim: Stating coverage as a floor prevents the independent-only density being read as total supply
pros.example: insurance's 0.83/10k is correctly read as saturated once uncounted captives are acknowledged

cons.claim: An acknowledged-but-unquantified undercount limits how precisely saturation can be stated
cons.example: without a roster the true insurance density is known to be higher but not by how much

failure_modes: reading an independent-only density as total supply and declaring white-space that captives fill
quantifying the undercount when only a directional gap is supportable
acceptance_tests: the catalog is stated as a floor, the uncounted supply categories are named, and the insurance and notary undercounts are explained with the roster confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a license roster or chain/captive census becomes available
a new uncounted supply category is identified

nodes.definition: Read the insurance sub-category as the most contested and, on a total-supply basis, saturated: six catalogued independents (CalWest, GDI, Tom Michael, Western Valley, Winton-Ireland Strom & Green, insureCAL) plus the uncatalogued captive brands make it the crowded sub-sector once captives are counted. Commoditized personal auto/home leaks to online and direct carriers, so differentiation runs on lines specialization (ag, commercial-auto/trucking, crop) and renewal-book defense. The defensible wedge is ag/commercial specialization plus a multi-carrier appointment set that incumbents' 20+-year tenure (CalWest's profile) already locks up; carrier appointments themselves are a barrier, since a new agency needs market access via a cluster/aggregator before it can quote competitively. Do not enter on commodity personal lines into an at-or-above-benchmark market.

excluded: the per-10k density figure (its own node)
the entry verdict (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an insurance supply or carrier-appointment norm changes

pros.claim: Reading insurance as saturated-once-captives-counted corrects the slightly-below-benchmark independent-only figure
pros.example: adding the captive State Farm/Farmers/Allstate offices pushes true density to or above the benchmark

cons.claim: Without a captive census the saturation call rests on an acknowledged-but-unquantified undercount
cons.example: the exact total agency density in Turlock is directional, not measured

failure_modes: recommending entry on commodity personal lines into a saturated market
ignoring that carrier appointments gate competitive quoting
acceptance_tests: the six independents are named, insurance is read as saturated on a total-supply basis, and the ag/commercial specialization wedge plus carrier-appointment barrier are stated
revisit_triggers: an insurance independent or captive opens or closes
a carrier-appointment or cluster-access norm changes
a commercial/ag-lines demand shift

nodes.definition: Read real estate as white-space at the brokerage-brand level but crowded at the agent level: four catalogued brokerage brands (Lifestyle Realty, Redwood Real Estate, Theis Realty Group, Valley Heritage Realty), each fronting a roster of 1099 agents, against hundreds of individual DRE agents county-wide plus national/portal competition (Zillow, Redfin, discount brokers) and thin 2024-25 transaction volume on a ~$465-475k median home. Boutique/community positioning (Lifestyle's model) is a viable brokerage-brand lane, but income is cyclical and split-diluted, and a new brokerage competes for the same finite ~once-a-decade transaction pool against incumbents who hold the referral networks. The open lane is a differentiated brokerage brand, not another agent; the agent tier is saturated and cyclically squeezed.

excluded: the per-10k density figure (its own node)
the entry verdict (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a brokerage count or transaction-cycle figure changes

pros.claim: Splitting brand-level white-space from agent-level saturation locates the only viable real-estate lane
pros.example: a community-boutique brand is open while 'another agent' competes in a saturated tier

cons.claim: Brand white-space is thin once cyclical volume and split dilution are priced in
cons.example: a 2024-25 thin-volume market drags the low end of brokerage GCI

failure_modes: reading the four-brand count as open white-space without the agent-tier saturation
ignoring the once-a-decade finiteness of the transaction pool
acceptance_tests: the four brokerage brands are named, brand-level white-space is distinguished from agent-level saturation, and the cyclical/split-diluted and referral-network caveats are stated
revisit_triggers: a brokerage brand opens or closes
a rate-cycle or transaction-volume shift
an agent-count or portal-competition change

nodes.definition: Read accounting/tax as moderate: independents sit near the US density benchmark (0.41 vs ~0.38/10k) but face a pincer — national chains plus free/DIY software (TurboTax/IRS free-file) on simple returns from below, and larger Modesto CPA firms on complex audit/advisory from above. The defensible middle is business/farm/multilingual clients with recurring bookkeeping and payroll: sticky, fee-tolerant, and hard for both chains and distant firms to serve. The catalogued three (Berger & Company, Charles Strand, Wahl, Willemse & Wilson) split structurally between a solo/small CPA and partner-plus-staff firms, which is itself a clue to their revenue bands. The wedge for an entrant is not another commodity 1040 shop but recurring business/farm advisory plus multilingual service.

excluded: the per-10k density figure (its own node)
the entry verdict (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an accounting supply or free-file/Modesto competitive factor changes

pros.claim: Framing accounting as a pincered middle locates the defensible recurring-advisory wedge
pros.example: business/farm bookkeeping and payroll resist both TurboTax below and Modesto CPAs above

cons.claim: The at-benchmark read undercounts chains and solo EAs, so true tax-prep density is higher
cons.example: H&R Block/Liberty and CSU-adjacent enrolled agents are not in the independent count

failure_modes: recommending a commodity 1040 shop into a chains-plus-free-file pincer
ignoring the solo-vs-partner structural split when reading revenue
acceptance_tests: the three accounting firms are named, the at-benchmark density and the chains-below/Modesto-above pincer are stated, and the business/farm/multilingual middle is named as the wedge
revisit_triggers: an accounting firm or chain opens or closes
a free-file/DIY-software policy or capability change
a Modesto-CPA competitive shift

nodes.definition: Read notary/immigration-doc and translation as the apparent white-space — lowest catalog density (0.14/10k) and the strongest demographic tailwind from the four communities — but constrained structurally, not competitively. Vega's Professional Services is the lone standalone catalog entry and even it survives only by stacking tax, notary, bookkeeping, payroll, real estate and translation. The format pencils only when bundled because the statutory ~$15/signature cap makes plain notarization volume-thin and the notario-fraud prohibition blocks the higher-margin legal-advice line; loan signings (~$75-$200) are the real notary margin driver. This is the clearest community-demand-supported niche a generic same-size town would not sustain and the hardest for Modesto/online to take, but the 'white-space' is real demand monetizable only through the multiservicios/gestoria bundle, not a green field for a standalone notary shop.

excluded: the statutory scope cap mechanism in detail (its own node)
the entry verdict (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an immigration-policy, fee-cap, or multiservicios-supply change

pros.claim: Reading notary white-space as bundling-only prevents recommending a standalone notary shop that cannot pencil
pros.example: Vega's survives by stacking lines, not on capped notary fees alone

cons.claim: Bundled-format demand is elastic to immigration policy and concentrated in specific communities
cons.example: USCIS/policy cycles swing immigration-doc volume independent of local demand

failure_modes: treating the 0.14/10k density as a green field for a standalone notary shop
ignoring that the fee cap and scope prohibition force the bundle
acceptance_tests: the apparent 0.14/10k white-space is stated, the bundling-only viability (Vega's archetype) is explained, and the loan-signing margin driver is named alongside the fee-cap constraint
revisit_triggers: an immigration-policy or USCIS-cycle shift
a multiservicios format opens or closes
a statutory fee cap or bonding requirement changes

nodes.definition: Model the two-sided leakage that caps the independent middle. Complex/high-value work — audits, commercial-risk placement, high-net-worth tax planning — migrates ~15 miles north to Modesto, the county seat with larger CPA firms, regional brokerages and full title/escrow infrastructure, capping the top. Simultaneously, commodity/price-sensitive work leaks online: TurboTax/IRS free-file on simple returns, Policygenius/eHealth on commodity insurance, Redfin/iBuyers/discount brokers on simple home sales, capping the bottom. The two drains leave Turlock independents the relationship-, language- and ag/business-specialized middle as the defensible core. The leakage is a reasoned estimate of behavior, not a measured figure; a Turlock-vs-Modesto referral/cross-shop study and online-penetration data would confirm it.

included: the relationship/language/ag middle as the defensible core
excluded: per-sub-category competitive reads (their own nodes)
the equilibrium count synthesis (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a Modesto cross-shop or online-penetration figure changes

pros.claim: Naming both leakage directions explains why independents hold only the middle, capping the count
pros.example: audits leave for Modesto while simple returns leave for TurboTax, leaving the relationship middle

cons.claim: Leakage is inferred from proximity and online substitutes, not measured, so its magnitude is uncertain
cons.example: without a cross-shop study the exact share of complex work going to Modesto is unknown

failure_modes: treating the leakage estimate as a measured figure
applying the top-leak logic to relationship/language work Modesto and online cannot take
acceptance_tests: both leakage directions are stated (complex to Modesto ~15 miles, commodity online), tied to capping the top and bottom, and flagged as a behavioral estimate with a confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a Turlock-vs-Modesto referral/cross-shop study
an online-penetration data release
a Modesto firm-capacity or title/escrow change

nodes.definition: Explain why a ~73k town supports roughly 14 nameable independents — not 30, not 5 — as a two-sided squeeze on a bounded demand pool with one demographic expander. Four caps hold the count near (or, counting captives, at) benchmark: a bounded local demand pool (a $82,995-median, 25,365-household town generates finite returns/policies/sales with no metro-scale commercial book); two-sided leakage to Modesto and online; licensing friction that slows but does not stop entry; and incumbent referral-network saturation that raises the effective cost of entry above the licensing cost. The one expander is the four-community demand for multilingual services that keeps the count from falling lower. Fourteen is read as an equilibrium where a finite pool of credentialed professionals meets a finite pool of transactions in an incumbent-saturated referral market, not a shortfall or a glut.

excluded: the per-sub-category density figures (their own node)
the leakage mechanism detail (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: one of the four caps or the community-demand expander shifts

pros.claim: Framing 14 as a four-cap-one-expander equilibrium resists both deficit and glut conclusions
pros.example: it explains why neither broad expansion nor contraction is the right read of the count

cons.claim: An equilibrium framing can imply false stability while licensing, leakage and community demand are moving
cons.example: treating 14 as fixed when a license-roster release could reveal a different true supply

failure_modes: reading the count as a deficit and recommending broad entry
ignoring that the equilibrium drifts as the caps and the expander change
acceptance_tests: the four caps and the one community-demand expander are each named and tied to the ~14-count outcome, with the credentialed-labor-meets-bounded-pool framing stated
revisit_triggers: a cap or the expander shifts materially (pool size, leakage, licensing, referral networks, community demand)
the independent count moves away from ~14

nodes.definition: Define the regulatory-scope gate that caps the notary/immigration line and can override a demand-true opening. In California a notary publico / immigration consultant is prohibited from giving legal advice (B&P 22440 et seq.); only attorneys or DOJ/EOIR-accredited representatives may, so a Vega's-type shop is limited to form-filling, translation and notarization, and the attorney/accredited-rep referral is a structural part of the workflow, not an optional add-on. The line also carries a $100,000 immigration-consultant bond (~$1,250-$4,000/2yr) and the ~$15/signature and $15-per-form fee caps. These are cited public facts. They are the single largest reason the demographic demand cannot scale into a higher-margin legal-advice business: the demand is real but the monetizable scope is statutorily capped, which is why the format only survives bundled.

included: the scope cap as a demand-override
excluded: the demand-side white-space read (its own node)
the composed entry verdict (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a statutory scope, bond, or fee-cap figure changes

pros.claim: Foregrounding the scope cap prevents a demand-true immigration-doc opening from being read as a high-margin legal practice
pros.example: the notario-fraud prohibition walls off legal advice no matter how strong the community demand

cons.claim: The statutory scope is itself subject to change and enforcement variation, so the gate is not perfectly fixed
cons.example: fee caps and bond requirements can be amended, shifting the gate

failure_modes: recommending a notary/immigration opening as if legal advice could be monetized
treating the immigration-consultant bond and fee caps as optional
acceptance_tests: the notario-fraud legal-advice prohibition, the $100k bond, and the fee caps are each stated as cited public facts and applied as an override on the notary/immigration white-space
revisit_triggers: a B&P statute, fee cap, or bonding requirement changes
an enforcement or accreditation-pathway change

nodes.definition: Enforce the binding honesty discipline across every dollar figure: per-business revenue is not public for these privately held independents, so no dollar figure is ever stated as an actual reported figure for a named business (CalWest, Berger & Company, Vega's, or any other). Every format dollar band is a labeled benchmark estimate (published per-unit benchmark x observable size signal) tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence word and a confirmation path; every high-gross band is paired with its gross-not-net cost reality; city/county/state/industry figures are cited public facts or labeled derivations; and carrier/lender/MLS/referral links are representative inference unless a cited source states the relationship (the Tom Michael Mercury-carrier listing is the one documented carrier link). Method, public source and confidence must travel with every number. This guardrail governs how all the sizing and structure nodes may be expressed.

included: the public-fact-vs-inference distinction for supplier/referral links
excluded: the specific band values
the saturation reads

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new dollar figure is introduced or an actual datum becomes available

pros.claim: A single explicit guardrail keeps every downstream number honest and auditable
pros.example: tagging every commission/GCI/fee band estimate-not-actual prevents any figure being read as an audited fact about a named firm

cons.claim: Heavy labeling can make the analysis read as hedged and lower its perceived usefulness
cons.example: a reader wanting a single firm revenue number is frustrated by a band tagged low-confidence

failure_modes: letting a format band attach to a named business as that business's revenue
stating a supplier/referral link as a confirmed contract rather than representative inference
acceptance_tests: every dollar figure is a labeled estimate or a cited public fact, no named-business actual revenue appears, each high-gross band carries its gross-not-net caveat, and supplier/referral links are marked inference unless a source states otherwise
revisit_triggers: a new node introduces a dollar figure
a public-fact source is added or updated
an actual revenue datum (e.g., a roster/CDTFA join) becomes available to replace an estimate

nodes.definition: Demonstrate the benchmark x size-signal method end to end on worked, auditable examples so the bands can be reproduced and challenged. Solo CPA: ~200 returns x ~$300 avg fee ~= $60k, scaling to ~$250k with light bookkeeping/payroll and more complex returns (the Charles Strand-profile floor-to-mid of ~$60k-$250k). Real-estate per-side: a ~$470k median home x ~2.73% listing-side commission ~= ~$12.8k gross per side, of which a 70/30 split leaves the agent ~$9k and the brokerage ~$3.8k, consistent with the ~$11k-$15k-per-side national benchmark. Insurance: an illustrative $2M premium book x a blended ~10% commission ~= $200k commission revenue, scaling up with multi-line/ag tenure toward the ~$300k-$2M+ band. Every worked figure is illustrative and estimate-not-actual, never a claim about a named firm; the arithmetic is shown only so a reader can audit the method, and the inputs (return count, book size, sides/yr) remain unknown for any specific business.

included: worked solo-CPA, per-side and insurance examples
excluded: the full band table (its own node)
the honesty-labeling rule (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark input or band is revised

pros.claim: Showing the arithmetic end to end lets a reader audit and challenge the method rather than trust a band
pros.example: a ~$470k home x 2.73% x 70% reproduces the ~$9k agent per-side figure transparently

cons.claim: Worked examples risk being mistaken for a specific firm's actual revenue if the illustrative framing is dropped
cons.example: the $2M-book insurance example could be misread as CalWest's book without the estimate-not-actual tag

failure_modes: a reader treating a worked example as a named firm's actual revenue
an arithmetic slip that makes the worked figure inconsistent with its stated inputs
acceptance_tests: at least three worked examples (solo CPA, real-estate per-side, insurance book) show their inputs and arithmetic, each tagged illustrative-and-estimate-not-actual, and each result lands inside its sub-category band
revisit_triggers: a benchmark rate or median-home-price input changes
a band is revised and a worked example must be re-derived

nodes.definition: Produce the entry go/no-go verdict for a given sub-category, composing the saturation read, the two-sided leakage, the competitive-structure white-space, and the regulatory-scope/referral-moat gate into one decision. The merged rule: do not enter insurance on commodity personal lines (saturated once captives are counted) or add another generic agent or commodity 1040 shop; the defensible headroom is ag/commercial insurance specialization, a differentiated real-estate brokerage brand, recurring business/farm/multilingual accounting advisory, and the multiservicios/gestoria bundle — each viable only after clearing its gate (carrier appointments and the referral-network moat for insurance, the once-a-decade transaction finiteness for real estate, and the notario-fraud scope cap plus $100k bond for immigration-doc). A demand-true opening that fails its gate is a no-go until the gate clears.

excluded: the per-sub-category competitive evidence (their own nodes)
the review cadence (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a saturation, leakage, or gate input to the verdict changes

pros.claim: Composing all reads into one verdict gives an actionable enter/avoid call instead of scattered signals
pros.example: the verdict says no to commodity personal-lines insurance but yes to ag/commercial specialization once appointments clear

cons.claim: A single verdict can over-simplify a sub-category whose demand and gate point opposite ways
cons.example: the multiservicios bundle has demand headroom yet still needs the scope-cap and bond cleared before a clean yes

failure_modes: issuing a yes on demand headroom while ignoring an unmet carrier-appointment, referral-moat or scope gate
recommending a saturated sub-category because a heritage or farm anchor looks durable
acceptance_tests: the verdict for a proposed sub-category combines its saturation read, leakage, white-space and gate status, names the do-not-enter formats, and refuses any demand-true but gated addition
revisit_triggers: a saturation read, leakage estimate, or gate feeding the verdict changes
a previously gated opening clears its gate

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the market reads current. A fixed refresh cadence (re-run on each major data release) plus material-change triggers — a CA DOI/DRE/CTEC license-roster release or a CDTFA/BLS occupational-data join (which would collapse the transaction pool, the density floors, and the revenue bands from estimates into measured figures at once), a census/ACS demographic refresh, a statutory fee-cap or bond change, a commission-rate-norm shift, a rate-cycle move in the home-sale market, an immigration-policy/USCIS-cycle swing, or a community-migration change — route the analysis back through TRANSACTION_POOL and the saturation reads. Without this loop the 2026-06-30 snapshot silently goes stale as rates move, immigration policy shifts, and incumbent referral networks deepen. The roster/CDTFA join is the single highest-leverage trigger.

included: re-entry into pool sizing and saturation
excluded: the initial market reads themselves
operator-level day-to-day decisions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

pros.claim: A trigger list with the roster/CDTFA confirmation keeps the lowest-confidence numbers on a path to resolution
pros.example: a license-roster release fires the loop and replaces the pool, density and band estimates with measured figures at once

cons.claim: Too-frequent refresh churns the reads without new signal, since most inputs update only annually
cons.example: re-sizing the pool monthly when ACS counts and benchmarks move yearly wastes effort

failure_modes: no cadence set so the snapshot ages silently past its rate/policy assumptions
ignoring a fired trigger (new roster data) and continuing on stale estimates
acceptance_tests: a refresh cadence and an explicit material-change trigger list exist, each routing back to TRANSACTION_POOL and the saturation reads, with the roster/CDTFA join named as the highest-leverage trigger
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse for how the inputs actually update

the per-10k density reads the catalog count against the population the pool is built on

the notary/immigration read decomposes the lowest density into the bundling-only white-space

the captive undercount is what turns the slightly-below insurance density into a saturated read
Modesto-and-online leakage causally creates the chains-below / Modesto-above pincer on accounting

the farm/business base is the recurring-advisory middle the accounting read names as defensible

the verdict consumes the brand-vs-agent real-estate read
the verdict consumes the pincered-middle accounting read

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_regulatory_scope_gate
conflict_axes.description: A sub-category can be demand-true white space yet be walled off by the notario-fraud scope cap, bonding, or carrier-appointment/referral moats, so the demand and feasibility views point opposite ways.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true opening as a no-go until its gate clears; demand never overrides the scope cap, bond, or appointment/referral moat

conflict_axes.name: gross_band_vs_net_income
conflict_axes.description: A high commission/GCI/fee gross band and the thin net after the labor-and-license cost stack cannot both describe a firm's earnings.
poles: read the gross band as earnings
read net after the cost stack
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the gross band is the revenue view; net is far lower after payroll, splits, E&O and software, so always pair the gross band with the cost reality

conflict_axes.name: independent_count_vs_total_supply
conflict_axes.description: Independents are the only catalogued supply, but captives, chains and bundled functions mean the true supply is higher, so the independent-only density understates saturation.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: read every density as a floor; insurance is saturated once captives are added even though the independent-only figure reads slightly below benchmark

conflict_axes.name: complex_leak_vs_local_specialization
conflict_axes.description: Modesto and online drains pull complex and commodity work away while the farm/community middle pulls specialized work toward local independents.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply leakage to commodity and complex work; hold the relationship/language/ag-business middle as the defensible local core

conflict_axes.name: licensing_friction_vs_referral_moat
conflict_axes.description: The licensing gate is real but surmountable, while the incumbent referral/in-force-book moat is the harder, often-underweighted barrier to entry.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat licensing as friction-not-wall and the referral/in-force-book as the binding moat that sets the effective cost of entry

conflict_axes.name: brokerage_brand_vs_agent_density
conflict_axes.description: Real estate looks like white space at the four-brand level but is saturated at the agent level, so a brand count and an agent count give opposite reads.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the agent count is the binding figure; brand white-space is viable only as a differentiated boutique, not as another agent

conflict_axes.name: community_demand_durability_vs_policy_elasticity
conflict_axes.description: The four-community demand is durable and defensible, yet the immigration-doc slice is elastic to USCIS/policy cycles that swing volume independent of local demand.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat community demand as durable for tax/notary/translation but flag the immigration-doc line as policy-elastic in any sizing

conflict_axes.name: estimate_labeling_vs_decisiveness
conflict_axes.description: Rigorous estimate-not-actual labeling protects honesty but can make the analysis read as too hedged to act on.
poles: label every figure as an estimate
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: label every figure but pair it with a confidence word and a confirmation path so the read stays actionable without overclaiming a named firm's revenue

conflict_axes.name: snapshot_stability_vs_cycle_drift
conflict_axes.description: The ~14 equilibrium reads as stable, but rate cycles, immigration policy, and deepening incumbent referral networks are moving the underlying forces.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the snapshot as a dated baseline but let the review loop, not assumption, decide when drift has moved the equilibrium

edge_cases.description: A format band is attached to a named business as if it were that business's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: a per-sub-category estimate is quoted next to CalWest, Berger & Company, or Vega's
edge_cases.mitigation: keep every band format-level and estimate-not-actual; never bind a dollar figure to a named business as fact

edge_cases.description: A high insurance commission or real-estate GCI band is read as net income
edge_cases.trigger: a gross commission/GCI figure is used without the cost stack
edge_cases.mitigation: pair the gross band with payroll ~40-60%, producer/agent splits, E&O and software before any net read

edge_cases.description: The full-CPA-firm band (~$400k-$1.2M+) is cited without its staff-count-unknown caveat
edge_cases.trigger: the lowest-confidence band is used as a solid figure in downstream sizing
edge_cases.mitigation: mark the full-CPA band lowest-confidence-staff-unknown and route to the roster/CDTFA confirmation

edge_cases.description: Insurance is read as below-benchmark and open because only independents are counted
edge_cases.trigger: the 0.83/10k independent-only density is treated as total supply
edge_cases.mitigation: add the uncatalogued captive offices and read insurance as saturated on a total-supply basis

edge_cases.description: A standalone notary shop is recommended on the 0.14/10k apparent white-space
edge_cases.trigger: the lowest density is read as a green field without the fee cap and scope prohibition
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the ~$15/signature cap and notario-fraud scope prohibition; the line pencils only bundled as a multiservicios

edge_cases.description: Real estate is read as open white space on the four-brand count
edge_cases.trigger: the brokerage-brand count is used without the agent-level density
edge_cases.mitigation: read the agent tier as the binding, saturated figure; only a differentiated boutique brand is open

edge_cases.description: Community demand is sized as durable while ignoring immigration-policy elasticity
edge_cases.trigger: the immigration-doc line is annualized on peak community demand
edge_cases.mitigation: treat tax/notary/translation demand as durable but discount the immigration-doc slice for USCIS/policy-cycle swings

edge_cases.description: Leakage to Modesto is treated as a measured figure rather than a behavioral estimate
edge_cases.trigger: a specific share of complex work is quoted as migrating to Modesto
edge_cases.mitigation: state leakage as a reasoned estimate of behavior with a cross-shop study as its confirmation path

edge_cases.description: A worked revenue example is mistaken for a named firm's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: an illustrative $2M-book or per-side calculation is read as CalWest's or a specific agent's figure
edge_cases.mitigation: tag every worked example illustrative-and-estimate-not-actual with unknown firm-level inputs

edge_cases.description: Vega's is double-counted by function across notary, tax and real estate
edge_cases.trigger: a multi-category multiservicios is tallied once per secondary category
edge_cases.mitigation: use primary category as the spine; the de-duplicated catalog total is 14, not a function-inflated count

edge_cases.description: A CA DOI/DRE/CTEC roster or CDTFA join arrives and contradicts the estimated pool and densities
edge_cases.trigger: measured license and tax-receipt data become available
edge_cases.mitigation: fire the review loop, replace the pool, density and band estimates with the measured figures, and re-derive the reads

workflow.description: Record the resident/household counts, median income, and farm-economy commercial base with cited magnitudes
workflow.gate: the household count, median income, and farm/commercial base each have a cited public-fact magnitude and a source confidence

workflow.description: Tie each of the four communities to the formats it anchors and name the licensing gates as friction-not-wall
workflow.gate: each of the four communities is tied to an anchored format and the per-sub-category licensing gates are named

workflow.description: Derive returns/policies/sales as households x frequency, with the calendar-locked finiteness and the roster/CDTFA confirmation path
workflow.gate: the pool is stated as an estimate-not-actual with derivation, finiteness, and confirmation path

workflow.description: State each sub-category's payment mechanism and per-unit benchmark, flagging rate-is-fact / application-is-estimate
workflow.gate: each sub-category's mechanism and cited per-unit benchmark are stated with the application-is-estimate caveat

workflow.description: Derive each band as benchmark x size signal, paired with its gross-not-net caveat and confidence word
workflow.gate: every band is estimate-not-actual with a size signal, confidence word, and gross-not-net pairing

workflow.action: Rank band confidence and work the math
workflow.description: Rank the bands by confidence and show worked solo-CPA, per-side and insurance examples that land in their bands
workflow.gate: the bands are confidence-ranked and at least three worked examples are shown, each tagged illustrative-and-estimate-not-actual

workflow.action: Read per-10k saturation and the coverage floor
workflow.description: Set each sub-category count against the 7.25 base and qualify every figure as a floor
workflow.gate: each sub-category has a per-10k density and a saturated/near/white-space read qualified as a floor

workflow.description: Give the saturated/crowded/moderate/white-space read for insurance, real estate, accounting and multiservicios
workflow.gate: each sub-category has a competitive read with its defensible wedge and gate named

workflow.action: Model leakage and the equilibrium count
workflow.description: Name the two-sided leakage and tie the four caps plus the one community-demand expander to the ~14 count
workflow.gate: the four caps and the one expander are named and tied to the ~14-count outcome

workflow.description: Combine saturation, leakage, white-space and the regulatory/referral gate into an enter/avoid call
workflow.gate: the verdict refuses any demand-true but gated addition and names the do-not-enter formats

workflow.action: Set the market review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the refresh cadence and material-change triggers routing back to pool sizing and saturation
workflow.gate: a cadence and a trigger list (roster/CDTFA highest-leverage) routing to TRANSACTION_POOL and saturation exist

priority_rationale: The demand base, community and farm demand, and licensed-labor supply are foundational because pool sizing, saturation, and the competitive reads all read from them; the transaction pool and commission/fee mechanics precede the per-format bands, the gross-net gap, the confidence ladder and the worked math they constrain; per-10k density and the coverage floor precede the per-sub-category competitive reads and the two-sided leakage; the equilibrium count aggregates the caps and the one expander; the revenue-honesty guardrail governs every dollar expression; and the entry go/no-go verdict plus the review loop come last because they compose all upstream reads into a decision and a self-correcting refresh.

dominance_rules.rule: The revenue-honesty guardrail dominates any pressure for a single decisive named-firm number
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so an over-decisive figure for a named firm would be a fabrication
dominance_rules.trigger: a request for a named business's revenue or a single firm market number
dominance_rules.action: answer only with a labeled estimate (benchmark x size signal) plus a confidence word and confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: The regulatory-scope gate dominates a demand-true notary/immigration opening
dominance_rules.rationale: the notario-fraud prohibition and bond cap the monetizable scope regardless of community demand
dominance_rules.trigger: an immigration-doc opening is judged attractive on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: mark it a no-go until form-filling/translation/notarization scope and the $100k bond are cleared and the legal-advice line is referred out

dominance_rules.rule: The gross-not-net pairing dominates a high-gross band read as earnings
dominance_rules.rationale: high commission/GCI/fees are gross and mostly consumed by labor-and-license costs and splits
dominance_rules.trigger: a gross band is used to characterize a firm's income
dominance_rules.action: apply the cost stack (payroll ~40-60%, splits, E&O, software) before any net read

dominance_rules.rule: True total supply dominates the independent-only density for saturation
dominance_rules.rationale: captives, chains and bundled functions make the catalog a floor, not total supply
dominance_rules.trigger: an independent-only density is used to declare white space
dominance_rules.action: add the uncounted captive/chain/bundled supply and read the density as a floor before any saturation call

dominance_rules.rule: The referral-network moat dominates the licensing cost for entry feasibility
dominance_rules.rationale: the in-force book and referral graph, not the license, set the effective cost of entry
dominance_rules.trigger: entry feasibility is judged on the license alone
dominance_rules.action: weight the incumbent referral/in-force-book moat and carrier appointments above the licensing friction

dominance_rules.rule: Agent-level density dominates the brokerage-brand count for real estate
dominance_rules.rationale: hundreds of DRE agents county-wide are the binding figure, not the four brands
dominance_rules.trigger: real-estate saturation is judged on the brokerage-brand count
dominance_rules.action: read the agent tier as the binding, saturated figure; allow only a differentiated boutique brand

dominance_rules.rule: The Modesto-and-online leakage dominates local demand math for commodity and complex work
dominance_rules.rationale: cross-shopping and online substitutes drain both ends regardless of local demand
dominance_rules.trigger: a complex or commodity opening is justified on Turlock demand alone
dominance_rules.action: cap the top and bottom via leakage and hold only the relationship/language/ag-business middle

dominance_rules.rule: A flagged low-confidence input dominates a confident downstream conclusion built on it
dominance_rules.rationale: a conclusion cannot be more certain than its weakest load-bearing input
dominance_rules.trigger: the transaction pool or a benchmark band carries a conclusion above its own confidence
dominance_rules.action: cap the conclusion's confidence at that of its weakest input and name the roster/CDTFA confirmation source

dominance_rules.rule: Community-demand durability dominates national/online substitution for relationship work
dominance_rules.rationale: language-and-trust demand is the hardest for Modesto and online players to take
dominance_rules.trigger: online or distant-firm substitution is applied to multilingual relationship work
dominance_rules.action: discount the substitution for tax/notary/translation relationship demand while still flagging immigration-policy elasticity

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size the transaction pool before estimating commission/fee mechanics or per-format bands
anti_rework_rules.prevents: deriving mechanics and bands against a pool that later moves, forcing a full re-derivation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every dollar figure estimate-not-actual at the moment it is written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later honesty sweep that must re-caveat figures already quoted as facts about a named firm

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every gross band with its cost stack when the band is built
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a gross-as-net misread that must be reworked once the labor-and-license costs are surfaced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Read saturation off primary category, noting the Vega's multi-category straddle, before counting
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a function-inflated count above 14 that must be re-tallied

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify every density as a floor and add the uncounted captive/chain supply the first time it is used
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a white-space conclusion that captives or chains then void, forcing a re-read

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply the regulatory-scope and bond gate while reading the notary/immigration white-space, not after recommending it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a standalone notary shop that the scope cap and fee cap then void

anti_rework_rules.rule: Flag the lowest-confidence bands (full CPA firm, bundled total) and carry their confirmation path the first time they are stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: every downstream market read inheriting an unflagged low-confidence band that must be re-marked

anti_rework_rules.rule: Name the roster/CDTFA confirmation path on every low-confidence dollar or density figure as it is stated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later pass to attach confirmation sources to numbers already published without them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Weight the referral-network moat alongside the licensing gate when reading entry feasibility
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a license-only feasibility call that must be redone once the incumbent moat is priced in

iteration_protocol.trigger: CA DOI/DRE/CTEC license rosters for the 95380/95382 ZIPs or a CDTFA/BLS occupational join becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the transaction pool, the density floors, and the per-format bands with measured figures and re-derive the reads
re-run the demand base and community/farm demand and re-size the transaction pool

iteration_protocol.trigger: a statutory fee cap, immigration-consultant bond, or licensing requirement changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-price the regulatory-scope gate and re-issue any affected entry verdicts

iteration_protocol.trigger: a commission-rate norm or producer/agent split shifts
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the commission/fee mechanics and re-derive the bands and worked examples

iteration_protocol.trigger: a firm opens or closes in the catalog
iteration_protocol.action: re-tally the densities and the affected competitive-structure read

iteration_protocol.trigger: a rate-cycle move or thin/thick home-sale-volume shift occurs
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the real-estate structure and the transaction pool

iteration_protocol.trigger: an immigration-policy or USCIS-cycle swing occurs
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the multiservicios white-space and its policy elasticity

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Turlock-vs-Modesto cross-shop or online-penetration study is done
iteration_protocol.action: re-estimate the two-sided leakage and the equilibrium count
